trajectory_summary: The call opens with low resistance and drifts into extended personal banter that the rep leans into rather than steering, ultimately landing a booked appointment almost as a byproduct of goodwill rather than deliberate structure. The rep skips several script anchors (bill flip, interest-reason use, clean channel confirmation) and the appointment closes on friendliness, not on a tight handshake.
outcome_dispute: The appointment has a day and time (Saturday the 21st at 8AM) but the channel is never disambiguated — the customer explicitly frames it as an in-person visit ('you guys can come and look at it') and the rep confirms with 'we got you for everything' rather than correcting to a phone consultation as the schema expects. This is booked on date/time but carries unresolved channel risk the v1 tag wouldn't capture.

observed_outcome.quote: But, yeah, we got you for next Saturday, the twenty first at 8AM.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time are locked, satisfying 'booked,' but the channel is genuinely ambiguous: the customer frames it as an in-person visit at 10:45 ('you guys can come and look at it') and the rep affirms broadly ('we got you for everything') without ever stating it's a phone appointment, so this is recorded as unclear rather than assumed in_person.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: The first month was 85. My next one is supposed to be 75, so I say $80.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Rep captured the figure and moved straight to the roof question ('Do you know what type of roof you have?') without acknowledging the number or tying it to the appointment's value; the flip should have landed right after 02:12.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: For my home? Nah. Never. And I I don't even think any because it's a new build. I don't think anyone has it yet. So that's why I was like, if I do it if I do get it, I wanna be the first. No offense.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The customer's initial answer at 01:36 ('Not really... just had a guy come knock on the door') was thin, but the richer first-mover motivation surfaced later at 03:07 under the prior-design question; the rep never returns to either statement to anchor the appointment.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: unresolved appointment channel + missing button-up mechanics
primary_coaching_focus.quote: So you guys can come and look at it and give me a quote and all that? Oh, yeah. We got you for everything.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The booking closes without correcting the customer's in-person expectation and without the hour-block/no-driving/handshake steps — this is the highest-risk gap because it directly threatens the appointment holding (show-rate) and creates a mismatch the closer will have to untangle cold.

key_moments.quote: I already talked to somebody from your trucking, but go ahead.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior Ion (or Ion-adjacent) contact and the rep never asks what was discussed or by whom, losing a free competitive/duplicate-lead intel opportunity.

key_moments.quote: Asphalt shingle, single, it's a metal?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep offers a list of roof types as a leading multiple-choice prompt rather than an open question, and the customer's uncertain answer ('I think it's, what you said, the second one') shows the data captured may not be reliable.

key_moments.quote: For my home? Nah. Never. And I I don't even think any because it's a new build. I don't think anyone has it yet. So that's why I was like, if I do it if I do get it, I wanna be the first. No offense.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers a first-mover motivation on a brand-new build — a strong intrinsic interest signal distinct from bill pain — but the rep never reflects it back or anchors the appointment to it.

key_moments.quote: The first month was 85. My next one is supposed to be 75, so I say $80.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands over an actual bill figure and a trend (85 down to 75), a natural hook, but the rep logs it and moves straight to the roof question with no acknowledgment or reflection.
